sections.h2: Who sends and collects Gordon County property tax bills?
sections.html:
The elected Tax Commissioner does both jobs. According to the county's office page, that office mails roughly 28,000 property tax bills a year and collects the county, county Board of Education and state property taxes. It also takes exemption applications, issues executions against delinquent taxpayers and sells vehicle tags.

Walk-in service is on the ground level of Government Plaza at 215 North Wall Street, Calhoun, GA 30701. Call 706-629-9242 on weekdays between 8:30 am and 5 pm. Mailed payments go to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703, and enclosing a stamped return envelope gets you a receipt.

sections.h2: What makes Gordon County different for a house seller?
sections.html:
Gordon County sits in northwest Georgia, and Calhoun is its seat of government. Georgia's legislature formed it on February 13, 1850 from parts of Cass (later Bartow) and Floyd counties, on land that had been Cherokee territory and included New Echota, the last seat of the Cherokee Nation. Cities are Calhoun, Fairmount and Plainville, and Resaca is a town. Wikipedia gives its size as 358 square miles, nearly all dry land.

Baugh Mountain and Horn Mountain rise inside the county, the eastern half drains to the Coosawattee River and most of the western half to the Oostanaula, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest lies within its borders. Neighbors include Murray, Whitfield, Gilmer, Pickens, Cherokee, Bartow, Floyd and Walker counties.

Interstate 75 runs through the middle, and the county has more interstate exits than any other Georgia county. US 41, US 411 and several state routes cross it. Manufacturing anchors the economy: Mohawk Industries, the flooring maker, is headquartered here, and Shaw Industries, Beaulieu, LG Chem and Kobelco Construction Machinery America have a presence too.

QuickFacts lists 61,701 residents for July 2025, growth of 7.2 percent since 2020. The 24,859 housing units include a 73.9 percent owner share, with a survey median value of $222,900 for owned homes. That figure is below the other two counties in the same QuickFacts table. The median household income is $63,650, drivers spend 25.3 minutes on the way to work, and 289 building permits were pulled in 2025.

sections.h2: When are Gordon County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
An administrator's report dated October 20, 2026 said the digest and collection order were expected from the state revenue department that day. The same report said bills would be sent before October 31 and fall due by the end of December. Georgia's default is December 20, and counties may adopt another date, so rely on the one shown on your own bill.

sections.h2: How do Gordon County tax payments and balances work?
sections.html:
Online payment goes through the county's tax payment site, which asks you to accept a disclaimer first. A credit card payment carries a 2.50 percent convenience fee charged by the processor, not by the county. Owners who want to skip it can mail a check to the post office box above. For delinquent bills more than seven years old, the page tells owners to contact the tax commissioner's office directly.

Request the payoff from the office and keep a written copy for the closing agent. Staff can say whether a parcel has more than one year outstanding.

The same disclaimer gives closing attorneys and staff an instruction worth following: a property may be under appeal even when the website does not show it, so call 706-629-9242 for the most accurate balance before closing. The county offers no warranty on the website's figures.

sections.h2: What can a Gordon County owner do about the assessed value?
sections.html:
Use the yearly assessment notice. Georgia's guidance requires the notice to explain how to appeal. A challenge to market value is mailed to the assessors' board and must be postmarked inside 45 days of the notice's mailing. The county bills about 28,000 properties, so a high value on your notice is worth checking against neighbors.

  • Keep the notice envelope, because the mailing date starts the clock.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses and any contractor repair estimates.
  • Ask the assessors' office which forms and evidence it prefers.
  • Ask the tax commissioner how an appealed parcel appears on the bill before you pay.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Gordon County?
sections.html:
Exemption applications go to the tax commissioner, and the state lets an owner apply once the house is a primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of the benefit. Not applying is treated as a waiver. Returns are due from the first of January to the first of April. An owner who returned or paid last year and then skips the return is deemed to have filed at last year's final value.

Vehicle and mobile home paperwork also runs through this office, since it issues county and city mobile home decals and transfers vehicle titles. A seller who is also moving a mobile home off the lot should ask what must be settled first.

The Georgia revenue department also says municipalities levy their own tax, billed by the city clerk unless the city and county combined billing. Calhoun, Fairmount, Plainville and Resaca residents should ask which bills they will receive. Calhoun also has its own city school system (Calhoun Primary, Elementary, Middle and High Schools), so a home within city limits may sit in a different district than one served by the county system. Ask the tax commissioner which school levy applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How does Georgia treat unpaid Gordon County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
After the 60 days that follow a bill's postmark, interest can accrue, and penalties may be added to unpaid balances. The tax commissioner issues executions against delinquent taxpayers, and a recorded execution sits on the title until it is paid. A refund for tax wrongly assessed or collected has to be requested inside three years after it was paid.

A seller with a balance should ask for the payoff in writing, give it to the closing attorney, and expect the title company to settle it out of the sale money. We buy Gordon County houses as-is for cash, including homes in Calhoun and the smaller towns along I-75 where an owner has older repairs, tenants or back taxes. A cash buyer still needs a clear title, so the payoff is handled the same way. If an heir received the house under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page lists what must be recorded before a sale.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Gordon County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the county's online payment site, or mail a check to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. The office is at 215 North Wall Street in Calhoun and takes calls at 706-629-9242.

faqs.q: How much did Gordon County lower its tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county reported a 7.7 mill rate for 2026, down from 9.042 mills in 2024 and 2025. Its report says the last lower rate was in 2002.

faqs.q: Does Gordon County charge extra for card payments?
faqs.a: Yes. The county page lists a 2.50 percent convenience fee on credit card transactions, charged by the processor. A mailed check avoids it.

faqs.q: Who can tell a closing attorney the real balance on a Gordon County parcel?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner's office, at 706-629-9242. The county warns that a parcel may be under appeal without the website showing it.

faqs.q: By when must a Gordon County homeowner file for homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The state's cutoff is April 1 of the first year the owner wants it, and skipping the application is a waiver. In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes the applications.
